definitions.explanation: A set phrase said when leaving home or the office. Literally means 'I will go and come back.' The response is {行|い}ってらっしゃい.

examples.japanese: じゃ、{行|い}ってきますね。
{学校|がっこう}に{行|い}ってきます。
{会社|かいしゃ}に{行|い}ってきます。{夜|よる}には{帰|かえ}ります。
examples.english: I'm going to work. I'll be back in the evening.

examples.japanese: {毎朝|まいあさ}{子供|こども}たちは「{行|い}ってきます」と{言|い}って、{学校|がっこう}に{出|で}かけます。
examples.english: Every morning, the children say 'I'm leaving' and head off to school.

notes: This is one of the most common daily expressions in Japanese. It is said when leaving home, the office, or any place you intend to return to. The phrase implies you will come back. The listener responds with {行|い}ってらっしゃい.
